column2: Pastoralists are people who depend on animals for their livelihood
They move from one place to another in search of pasture and water

column3: Gujjars and Bakarwals of Jammu and Kashmir

column2: In summer they move to highlands
In winter they come down to plains
They depend on milk, meat, wool, and animals for transport
British wanted to control grazing lands
Pastoralists had to pay to graze animals
British considered grazing lands as wasteland
Lands were given to farmers and planters
Some pastoral groups were labeled as criminals
They were forced to live in fixed villages
Maasai lived in Kenya and Tanzania
They were forced into small reserves
Governments tried to modernize animal rearing
